claim: The index adds predictive accuracy beyond the prespecified comparison model, on held-out configurations.
decision_rule: Supported if the lower limit of the bootstrap interval on the added cross-validated R-squared exceeds 0. Supports: the index is a USEFUL SUMMARY INDEX carrying information the listed quantities do not. Does NOT support: a distinct mechanism.

claim: The index still adds accuracy on process families it was not fitted on.
decision_rule: As V1, fitting on the jump family and scoring on switch and drift. Failure here with V1 supported means the index summarizes within a process but does not transfer.

claim: The added accuracy survives the uncertainty of estimating the index from pilot paths.
reading: within the noise of estimating the index
decision_rule: As V1, with pilot paths resampled inside each configuration resample. A V1 supported and V3 not means the apparent gain is within the noise of measuring the index.

claim: Holding simple uncertainty measures close, configurations with a lower index do better.
decision_rule: Matched pairs close in standardized log sigma and log(1 + tau) and far apart in the index. Supported if the interval on the mean within-pair difference lies above 0.

claim: Holding the index close, the underlying process does not matter.
reading: sufficiency not supported: matched pairs differ by about as much as the outcome varies
decision_rule: Matched cross-family pairs close in the index. The index is a SUFFICIENT summary only if the mean absolute within-pair difference is small relative to the spread of the outcome. This claim is reported, never asserted: a large difference is evidence against sufficiency, not against usefulness.
